correctness.rationale: For binary linear indexed one-grain channels the zero-or-one overwrite output ball differs from each source in at most one noninitial coordinate. One-flip competitors number N=n-1; nonadjacent two-flip competitors are unequal pairs among derivative bits, minus adjacent derivative transitions, giving k(N-k)-b; adjacent two-flip competitors contribute k-t_1. The sum is N+k(N-k+1)-t_1-b. Derivative runs with given k and initial bit have precisely the four binomial-composition multiplicities in the RESULT; the constant derivatives are handled separately. Handshaking gives the edge count, and minimal penalty t_1+b proves the monotone derivative maximum with all n=1/2 boundary cases. Independently enumerated every distinct channel ball and confusable pair through length 8, checking every degree and edges 0,2,10,36,112,320,864,2240. Universal formulas rely on disjoint combinatorial cases, not finite testing.
